correctness.rationale: CRT and surjective reduction of SL₂(ℤ) give the full product over 8,3,5. Surjectivity follows by elementary generation over each local ring (one entry of a unimodular column is a unit), lifting the elementary entries via CRT. In SL₂(F₃) the upper triangular subgroup is exactly the signed unipotent subgroup of order 6. The other two chosen local subgroups are central, so the quotient in Γ₀(3) is the product of the local scalar quotients of sizes 96 and 60. All groups contain −I. The Γ₀(3) coset action on P¹(F₃) gives a fixed point and a 3-cycle for the order-three generator and for the cusp generator, and two 2-cycles for the order-two generator; hence the base has one order-three point, two cusps and genus zero. The traces allowed mod 8 exclude noncentral elliptic elements upstairs. In the standard conjugated translation both off-diagonal entries are k times squares of a primitive cusp vector; at each of 2 and 5 one square is a unit, so the scalar conditions force 8|k and 5|k. At 3 the lower entry forces 3|k just when c is nonzero mod 3. Thus the widths are 40 and 120, with relative inertia 40 at both cusps of widths 1 and 3. Normality gives fibers of sizes 1920,144,144. The full coset-action core has local parts of sizes 4,2,2: at 3 upper and lower signed unipotents intersect in ±I; the other factors stay central. This gives the claimed geometric monodromy and a torsion-free core curve of index 69120 with 576 cusps of width 120, hence genus 5473. Riemann–Hurwitz in the relative cover gives 1777. Independent exact replay with node /workspace/reviews/evidence/exact-crosschecks.js builds the local coset permutations, obtaining the all-3 and all-2 cycles and the 144 cycles of each width over j=∞; it also verifies local orders 3,3 and 8,5 for the relative generators. The source checker was inspected, not run. The notation Q₈ here means the defined order-96 quotient, not the quaternion group; nothing here determines the abstract curve's full automorphism group or an arithmetic descent.

value.rationale: The curve is intrinsically motivated, and the geometry is correctly described, but this narrow result is a direct extraction from the already specified product subgroup. Write Γ=K∩Γ₀(3), with K the kernel of the two central local quotients at 8 and 5. The regular intermediate quotient is then just the pullback of X_K→X(1) along X₀(3)→X(1). At 3 this is the standard four-point projective action; at 8 and 5 all nontrivial action is in regular quotient factors. Thus the degree and deck group are the factor orders, the relative cusp inertia is the scalar modulus 8·5 for either base cusp, and the Galois closure replaces the stabilizer of a projective point by the action kernel. The partitions and genera are standard arithmetic consequences of that same coset decomposition. This is not a case where a necessary exact invariant had to be resolved by a new classification, argument about the given curve, or nontrivial exact computation. The record does not give a further geometric or representation-theoretic consequence that would supply a distinct mathematical reason for this routine specialization. Value fails on mechanical implication, not on the size of the genus or on access to a table.
